details.label: Discussion
details.text: Scattered supercells and multicells continue to track across central SD with a history of producing measured severe gusts. MRMS mosaic radar trends suggest that some weakening of the ongoing storms has taken place over the past hour or so, casting some uncertainty to the long-term severe potential. Nonetheless, these storms are preceded by a favorable thermodynamic and kinematic environment. The 00Z ABR observed sounding depicted a buoyant airmass and no MLCINH, with nearly 2000 J/kg MLCAPE amid an elongated hodograph with over 30 kts of effective bulk shear. The 00Z mesoanalysis also depicted similar conditions present across most of eastern SD. Such conditions would support a continued severe gust threat into the evening hours. As such, convective trends will continue to be monitored for the possibility of a Severe Thunderstorm Watch issuance

details.label: Summary
details.text: Isolated damaging wind gusts are possible into the evening. The severe wind threat is expected to remain too isolated for watch issuance

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Numerous thunderstorms have developed along a surface boundary across the region with over 3000 J/kg of MLCAPE (per RAP-based mesoanalysis). Although these storms are developing in a weak-shear environment, the thermodynamic environment supports a threat of wet microbursts. As these storms pulse up and subsequently collapse, damaging wind gusts will be possible over the next couple of hours. Cold-pool clustering, as storms push to the southeast, may enhance the damaging wind threat. Given the isolated spatiotemporal severe-weather threat (ending shortly after dark), a severe-thunderstorm watch is unlikely
